Five of the ten organisms added to spike_P0 were detected and five were missed. The test was a species-level (S) clade read count of at least 10, from `data/spike_P0.report.gz` checked against the spike_P0 rows of `truth/spike_manifest.tsv`.

| Organism | Pairs added | Species clade reads | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pseudomonas aeruginosa | 40,000 | 811 | detected |
| Enterococcus faecalis | 40,000 | 6,457 | detected |
| Escherichia coli | 4,000 | 72 | detected |
| Staphylococcus aureus | 4,000 | 54 | detected |
| Lactobacillus fermentum (listed in the report as Limosilactobacillus fermentum) | 40 | 26 | detected |
| Salmonella enterica | 400 | 4 | missed |
| Bacillus subtilis | 40 | 2 | missed |
| Listeria monocytogenes | 400 | no species row (only the genus *Listeria*, 315 reads) | missed |
| Saccharomyces cerevisiae | 40,000 | not in the report | missed |
| Cryptococcus neoformans | 4,000 | not in the report | missed |

- **Reads stopping at genus level:** many reads were assigned to the genus rather than the species. For example, most Pseudomonas reads (15,356) and Enterococcus reads (21,857) sit directly on the genus. Detection counts only the species row, so this lowers the numbers but doesn't change any result.
- **Fungi absent:** the report has no fungal entries at all. That includes Saccharomyces cerevisiae, added at the highest level (40,000 pairs). The database used was probably bacteria-only, but the report can't confirm that.
